Bankrupt By Beanies (2009) - A short documentary about a family who went bankrupt spending $100k on Beanie Babies

The real interesting part of beanie babies that most people miss is that beanie babies is a marketing work of art. Believe it or not, the marketing plan for beanie babies was created before the idea of a beanie baby. The beanie baby toy was simply able to fulfill the role of the marketing plan. Here was the basic goals of the marketing plan:

Product needs to be cheap: The goal was to allow children to be able to afford them with their allowance. No need for mom's approval and they were cheap enough to be impulse buys.

Product only sold at small retailers: An item sold at a boutique mom&pop store gave the illusion that the item was more valuable. If the item was sold at WalMart or Target, it would give the impression that the beanie babies were mass produced.

Personification: Every beanie baby had a name so children could connect better with the toy.

Privacy: The owner's were rarely interviewed which created a sense of mystery around the toys.

Surprise: The beanie baby company would immediately stop production of certain beanie babies which instantly increased their value due to perceived scarcity. Likewise, beanie babies with "production flaws" would be created and sold randomly (beanie babies with flaws were rarer and therefore had a higher resell value). This gave the illusion that someone could buy a random beanie baby and it could be worth thousands!

Condition: The company stressed to consumers that to preserve the condition of the toy, they need to protect the condition of the toy by using plastic ID protectors or placing the beanie babies in plastic cases. This was simply a tactic to create an additional revenue stream.

False Messaging: The Ty company released news that Beanie Babies would be discontinued at the end of 1999 and released a beanie baby called "the end." Consumers were carried away in a frenzy and tried to buy every beanie baby they could find. In 2000, production restarted with a beanie baby called "the beginning."
